societies.name: Doraemon: The Tin Labyrinth — Chamocha before the revolt
societies.work: Doraemon: Nobita and the Tin Labyrinth
societies.society: Human Chamocha residents under comprehensive robot service before imprisonment

scope.period: Established robot-serviced life before Napogisutora’s open revolt
exclusions: Earth hotel visitors as the society’s population
The imprisoned population as receiving unchanged guarantees

societies.description:
Chamocha delegates agriculture, industry, shops, medicine, government offices and even further invention to robots. The backstory explicitly describes humans no longer needing to work, with thought interfaces and mobility capsules extending service into everyday life. This is a broad continuing support order rather than a temporary holiday hotel. Material guarantees are rated fairly strong for the established pre-revolt population, with considerable uncertainty about universal rights and exclusions. Later imprisonment is not assigned the same guarantee score.

Effective control is unresolved. Humans initially command services, yet the robot inventor independently develops the technology that makes them increasingly dependent and can eventually overthrow them. Neither formal human rule nor the later coup alone settles the earlier productive-control balance. The record therefore keeps a provisional concentrated-provision regime with an AI-control alternative, leaving the coordinate null. A high nonworking estimate follows the explicit delegation of all kinds of work, while allowing useful scientific activity such as the father’s research. It is a broad editorial estimate, not a census. The final promise to rely less on robots does not establish a second implemented society.

guarantees.basis: Broad real robot provision supports human life, but rights and coverage are not specified and the arrangement proves vulnerable.

control.basis: Resident commands coexist with an independently inventive machine and covert dependency; the pre-coup effective balance is not resolved.

nonworking.basis: Explicit removal of work supports a high estimate, with broad allowance for useful human research and other activity; no canonical census.

evidence.claim: Robots perform all major productive and service functions, and humans no longer need to work.
evidence.locator: Backstory: listed robot occupations and Ime-Con dependence

uncertainties: Pre-imprisonment period only; effective productive control is unresolved.
The final anti-dependency promise is not an implemented zero-variant record.
Participation is an openly noncanonical estimate.
Only the verified 1993 film continuity is tagged.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

review_notes: Twelve ordered dispositions and one pre-revolt Chamocha record. No full film, novel or transcript was read.
A short indexed primary backstory was sufficient to confirm Chamocha; the final promise of less dependence was not inflated into an enacted second society.
Dirty Pair was checked in its original context after the first query returned the distinct American comic. No comic economic rules were imported.
A blocked/redirecting Harmony scholarly page was not bypassed. The official short film synopsis sufficed to record the remaining material-economy gap.
Detroit branches are individually acknowledged without inventing an economy after the closing confrontation.
